name: Sabad
title: One of the conspirators against King Joash
summary: Sabad (also known as Josabad) was the son of an Ammonite woman named Shimeath. He was one of two servants who conspired against and killed King Joash of Judah, who had abandoned the Lord after the death of priest Jehoiada. Sabad's action was part of God's judgment on Joash for his apostasy and for killing the prophet Zechariah, son of Jehoiada.

keyEvents.title: Joash's Apostasy
keyEvents.description: After the death of priest Jehoiada, King Joash turned away from the Lord and began to worship idols, which ultimately led to his judgment.

keyEvents.title: The Murder of the Prophet Zechariah
keyEvents.description: King Joash ordered that Zechariah, son of priest Jehoiada, be stoned in the temple court because he prophesied against the king's sin. This provoked God's wrath.

keyEvents.title: The Aramean Attack on Judah
keyEvents.description: The Lord sent the Aramean army against Judah and Jerusalem as punishment, and they inflicted great damage and destruction on Joash.

keyEvents.title: Conspiracy Against King Joash
keyEvents.description: Zabad, son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad, son of Shimrith the Moabite woman, conspired against King Joash while he was ill after the Aramean attack.

keyEvents.title: The Murder of King Joash
keyEvents.description: Zabad and Jehozabad killed King Joash on his bed. He was buried in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings. His son Amaziah became king in his place.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in 2 Kings
keyEvents.description: In 2 Kings, the same events are recorded, where Zabad's name appears as Jehozabad, son of Shimeath, one of the two who struck down King Joash.
